methods.label: Bound the fifth number
methods.explanation:
When nine numbers are arranged from smallest to largest, their median is the fifth number. Among the given entries, the five numbers \(3,5,5,7,8\) are all at most \(8\). Thus, regardless of the three missing numbers, the fifth number cannot exceed \(8\).

This bound can be reached. Choose the missing integers to be \(10,11,12\). The complete sorted list is
\[
3,5,5,7,8,9,10,11,12,
\]
and its fifth number is \(8\). Therefore the largest possible median is \(8\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
